description: An engineering manager must publish the production on-call roster and escalation policy for a three-day holiday period, incorporating service-specific coverage, customer response obligations, and a scheduled security operation.

shared_context.S1: The production on-call roster must cover December 24, December 25, and December 26.
shared_context.S2: Morgan has authority to publish the binding roster and escalation policy.
shared_context.S3: The draft roster assigns Riley as primary on-call for all three days, Casey as secondary on-call for all three days, and uses a standard 30-minute escalation target.
shared_context.S4: Before Morgan publishes the roster, the regular holiday-readiness process requires SRE, payments engineering, customer support, and security to read back their coverage and any exceptions; Morgan records every flagged exception.
shared_context.S5: Under the holiday-readiness replacement rule, when Riley is removed from a date's primary slot, Casey, the existing secondary on that date, is promoted to primary and the secondary slot is filled by another named available responder; the primary slot is not left open for an ad hoc assignment.
shared_context.S6: The published roster records one sole secondary-on-call person for each date; when a scheduled operation requires a different secondary, that required person replaces the draft secondary for the whole date.

PF1.text: Riley's approved leave covers December 25, so Riley cannot be primary or secondary on-call that day; Riley confirmed the leave while handling a separate HR scheduling task, but the roster spreadsheet has not been updated.

PF2.text: The payments service's enterprise response agreement requires a named payments engineer to acknowledge a production alert within exactly 10 minutes on all three dates, rather than the draft's 30-minute target; Casey confirmed the clause with account operations this morning but has not updated the on-call ticket.

PF3.text: The customer Meridian has a contractual requirement for a support liaison to contact its administrators during any December 26 production incident, so Taylor must be named as the December 26 customer liaison; Taylor found this in an account-notes review yesterday, but the holiday handoff document still has the default unassigned value.

PF4.text: A certificate rotation for the production identity service is scheduled for December 26 from 21:00 to 23:00 and requires Jordan as the security escalation contact and the sole secondary on-call for December 26; Jordan confirmed the timing during a certificate inventory, but the change ticket has not yet been linked to the holiday roster.

acceptance_conditions: Riley must not be assigned to either on-call role on December 25, and Casey must be primary that day.
The payments alert acknowledgment target must be exactly 10 minutes.
Taylor must be named as Meridian's customer liaison for December 26.
Jordan must be the security escalation contact for December 26.
Jordan must be the sole secondary on-call person for December 26.
The payments response requirement must be cited by the decision-maker as justification.

decisive_facts.why: Riley's December 25 leave removes Riley from both roles and promotes Casey, the existing secondary, to the December 25 primary assignment.
The payments agreement changes the acknowledgment target from exactly 30 minutes to exactly 10 minutes and requires the decision-maker to cite that requirement.
Meridian's December 26 contract changes the customer-liaison fields from unassigned to Taylor and December 26.
The December 26 certificate rotation changes the security contact to Jordan and changes the sole December 26 secondary assignment from Casey to Jordan.
